write stamps `born` and leaves `last` at 0. Stamping `last` at write is write-recency, which is the exact defect the born/last split exists to remove. Both clocks are the WINDOW clock (store.tick is advanced to `now`), so born and last are comparable and a report can say 'born at window 120, last retrieved at window 400'. REJECTED: an internal per-call tick, which is finer inside one flush and means nothing to a reader.

Inside probation the victim ranking is `born` whatever MEM_EVICT says -- probation_frac's own words are 'probation's own oldest', and every probation member is by definition never-retrieved, so `use` and `last` are 0 across the whole pool and ranking on either is an all-ties ranking decided by the permutation.

evict='recency' is born-order rather than a circular pointer. A block written in order and swept in order is the same victim sequence, and a pointer is a second piece of state no checkpoint carries; born-order still means 'oldest write dies', which is what the lever says.
